agree.reason: A skeptical HR manager sees signed training records, two clean state audits, a cut from 20 to 12 hours and a GMP course with a set end date, so she would probably grant a phone screen, although leaving out interview availability gives her less reason to call quickly.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the unsupported claim about halving training time and states every number accurately, though 'The teaching itself works' credits the AP pass-rate rise to her alone, and 'keep everything GMP requires' implies GMP knowledge she doesn't have yet.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the seven injury-free years but leaves the strongest figures unstated: 20 to 12 hours is a 40% cut, and 41% to 58% is a 17-point gain.

right_comparison.reason: It never sets her against the realistic alternative, a candidate with GMP experience but no record of cutting training hours or passing audits, so the reader has to make that comparison herself.

qualification.reason: The gaps are hedged with dates she can check: the GMP course ends May 2, the contract ends June 14 and she can start then, and the LMS gap is stated plainly, though nothing says what happens if the course slips.

objections.reason: It meets the teacher-without-plant-experience objection head on with audited signed records and the GMP enrollment, and raises no objection the facts already answer, although the LMS gap is only acknowledged, not reduced.

fit.reason: It is a one-page cover letter as asked, but it is not ready to send, because the contact line, the date and the whole 'why Calder' paragraph are still placeholders.
